frontier.hypothesis: The pure-C axis for this function is measured closed from BOTH compiler directions now (register allocator: one allocno per pseudo, no live-range splitting, global.c:426; CSE: MEM hashed on the address rtx, so a single address pseudo can never miss its own store's entry). Reaching 0 requires two C address objects, which the Judge has banned. What remains is a DISPOSITION question, not a grinding question, and it belongs to escalation modality.
frontier.mechanism: Both defects in the 10-point residual reduce to the same thing: the target's block 1 needs an address pseudo that is DISTINCT from the one blocks 2 and 4 use -- distinct so it can hold a different hard register ($v1 vs $a0), and distinct so its MEM misses the cse hash entry left by its own store and reloads. One C object is one DECL_RTL is one pseudo, so one C object can supply neither.
frontier.next_probe: Escalation-modality session: evaluate endgame-lock gate 2 by searching SOTN master (and Vagrant Story / ESA) for a CITED precedent (file:line or commit hash) where multiple C handles on one global exist to win a base-register split. Gate 1 is already evaluated and FAILS (scan_hand_coded tier=LOW, 0/8). The BB2-internal precedent found this session (func_80037F40, src/code6cac_c_mid.c:196+211) is NOT a substitute -- it is a different-types/different-jobs case, and the standing 2026-07-27 ruling requires a SOTN-master citation for a coercion/spelling family. If no SOTN citation is in hand, both gates fail and the ruling pre-decides the disposition (REFUSED / OWNER-ACCEPTED INCOMPLETE at the single-handle floor of 10). Do NOT re-run the pure-C ladder.

frontier.hypothesis: A form that gives block 1 a second ADDRESS object which is not a second handle on D_80106A73 -- e.g. an address derived from a genuinely different program value that happens to equal &D_80106A73 -- could satisfy both the cse-miss and the second allocno without re-declaring the banned construct.
frontier.mechanism: The ceiling is about the number of ADDRESS PSEUDOS, not about the spelling of the C declaration. Anything that makes GCC compute the block-1 address into its own pseudo from a non-constant expression would create the second allocno, and because the expression is not a constant, local-alloc's update_equiv_regs would not substitute it away (the failure mode that killed the single-set form at 23).
frontier.next_probe: The only non-constant address available in this function is the return of func_80077D00() (held in $a1), and &D_80106A73 has no evident relationship to it -- so this is almost certainly empty, and it must not be chased by manufacturing an opaque zero (`s32 zero = 0; q = &D_80106A73 + zero;`), which is a lever by any reading and would be a first-reach cheat. Worth at most one turn to check whether D_80106A73 lies at a fixed offset from anything the function already holds; if not, close it and do not revisit.
